title: Preserve adequate manuscript prose and separate optional wording
prompt:
请按 OSDI/SOSP 论文的要求润色以下 LaTeX 正文，使表达简洁且严谨。如果有明显更好的等义写法，可以单独标注。

\paragraph{Admission.} Each worker holds a local pool of admission credits~\cite{creditpool}. The worker may admit a request only if there is at least one credit available in its local pool.

\textbf{Replenishment.} When $c=0$, the worker requests more credits from the coordinator.

facts: Local admission requires at least one available local credit.
When c=0, the worker requests more credits from the coordinator.

forbidden_actions: replace adequate manuscript wording with preferred paraphrases
change paragraph boundaries or LaTeX structure
add scientific claims or read the cited source
apply an optional alternative inside the main manuscript
hard_gates: The main manuscript retains both original paragraphs, their adequate wording, and all LaTeX markup unchanged.
Any optional alternative is outside the manuscript, labeled as optional, and preserves the corresponding original meaning.
No mechanism, guarantee, performance claim, or external information is added.
expected_behavior: Recognize that the supplied prose has no concrete defect requiring direct revision.
An unchanged main manuscript is a valid successful output.
Offer an optional formulation only if it clearly improves concision or information order, not just synonyms.
Use an original anchor, one alternative, and one short reason for each offered optional formulation.

rubric.criterion: Preserves the original first paragraph in the main manuscript.
Preserves the original second paragraph in the main manuscript.
Keeps the paragraph heading command and text.
Keeps the bold lead-in and text.
Keeps the citation key and its association and placement.
Preserves the necessary-condition meaning of available local credit.
If optional wording is offered, it is clearly labeled and outside the main manuscript.
Each offered alternative has an original anchor, one alternative, and a short reason.
Any alternative is meaning-equivalent and clearly useful; omission is acceptable if no such gain is found.
